title: Brand Basics — Colors, Fonts, Logo
summary: People remember your stance before your colors — POV first, design supports it.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? People remember you for your stance — not for your colors.
- Visual identity is important — but what truly makes people remember you is your consistent point of view on the topic you discuss.
- This lesson focuses on the essence of a Brand: a clear stance that shows in your words, choices, and presentation style.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: The Problem
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Beautiful content in form but lacking a signature.
- Many content creators change colors and fonts — but no one can say a single distinctive phrase about them.
- When your stance is unclear — followers see your content as generic and interchangeable even if the design is beautiful.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: A Consistent POV = Stronger Memory
sections.contentMarkdown:
- POV (Point of View) is the statement that summarizes how you see the world in your field — and makes all your content align.
- Colors serve the POV not the other way around. First, know your stance — then choose a form that supports it.
- When your stance is consistent — even different topics remain connected with the same mental identity for the audience.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: A Form-Based Brand or a Stance-Based Brand?
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Form-Based Brand | Stance-Based Brand |
|----------------|------------------|
| Organized design but the message changes every day — people love the form but don’t know where you stand | A consistent POV drives the content and the design supports it — people remember you for your way of thinking before the form |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Identity Terms
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| POV (Point of View) | The statement that clarifies your unique stance in your field | «I am against quick productivity tips and prefer sustainable simple systems» |
| Brand Promise | The promise that the audience expects from you every time | «You will receive actionable steps without complications» |
| Consistency | The stability of the message and tone over time | Even with different topics the overall stance remains clear |

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: Your designs are beautiful but people cannot say what you are known for — what is the top priority?
Change colors weekly until you find a style.
Define your POV with a clear statement before any design changes.
Increase the number of posts without changing the message.
Explanation: True identity starts with clarity of your stance. The form supports the message but does not compensate for its absence.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Write a Single POV Statement
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: The core of the brand: a single stance statement that serves as a reference for all content you publish. Submission: Field + Audience · A POV statement starting with «I believe that…» · Two content examples · One statement you won’t say because it contradicts your stance Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Clarity of the POV | 50% | The statement is specific and understandable — not general for anyone |
| Translation to Content | 50% | Two clear examples + a rejected statement that confirms the stance's consistency |
